# SQB AI Site — Final Adversarial Security Audit

**Scope:** Authorized owner audit of the SQB AI corporate site (`site/`, Next.js 14 / Prisma / Neon Postgres / NextAuth).
**Method:** Source review plus safe live probing against the local dev server, multiple independent reviewers with adjudicated severities.

---

## 1. Executive Summary

The application has **one catastrophic, unauthenticated, trivially-exploitable vulnerability** (path traversal in `/api/media/[key]`) that leaks the full `.env` — including the database password, the NextAuth signing secret, and the Telegram bot token. This single bug collapses the entire security model: with the leaked `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` an attacker forges admin sessions; with `DATABASE_URL` they own the production database directly. **Every secret in `.env` must be treated as compromised and rotated immediately.**

Beyond that, the app ships with no defense-in-depth: no security headers, no brute-force protection on admin login, documented default admin credentials checked into the repo, a rate limiter that is trivially bypassed by spoofing `X-Forwarded-For`, unauthenticated DB-writing endpoints, and a `force-dynamic` homepage that re-runs 10 DB queries on every request.

### Risk posture: **CRITICAL — do not treat as production-ready until the path-traversal bug is fixed and all secrets rotated.**

### Findings by adjudicated severity

| Severity | Count | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| **CRITICAL** | 1 | Path traversal → arbitrary file read → full `.env` / secret exfiltration → DB + admin takeover |
| **HIGH** | 5 | Missing security headers; no login brute-force protection; default admin creds in repo; contact rate-limit bypass + unbounded Map; stored XSS via SVG upload (one reviewer track) |
| **MEDIUM** | ~8 (deduplicated classes) | `/api/track` unauthenticated DB-write flooding; stored SVG XSS (admin-gated); homepage read-amplification; PII retention/consent gap; Telegram-fetch no-timeout; input validation gap |
| **LOW** | 3 | Flat admin privilege model (no RBAC); `createProject` trusts client id; login timing oracle |

> Note on duplication: the path-traversal issue was independently confirmed by **8 reviewers**; the SVG-XSS, `/api/track`, login brute-force, default-creds, and contact rate-limit issues each appear multiple times. They are consolidated below into one finding per root cause, with the **highest defensible adjudicated severity** retained.

## 2. CRITICAL & HIGH Findings

### 🔴 CRITICAL-1 — Unauthenticated path traversal in `/api/media/[key]` → arbitrary file read → full secret exfiltration

**What it is.** The dynamic media route passes the raw, URL-decoded `params.key` straight into a filesystem read with no sanitization, normalization, or containment check. A URL-encoded `../../` escapes the uploads directory and reads any file the Node process can access — including `.env`.

**Where.**
- `site/app/api/media/[key]/route.ts:8` — `const result = await readImage(params.key);` (no auth, no validation)
- `site/lib/storage.ts:77-79` —
  ```ts
  const file = path.join(process.cwd(), "public", "uploads", key); // key UNSANITIZED
  const data = await fs.readFile(file);
  ```
- `site/middleware.ts` — matcher is `["/admin/((?!login).*)", "/admin"]`; `/api/media` is **not** protected.

**Proof (live, localhost:3000).**
```
GET /api/media/..%2f..%2f.env            -> HTTP 200, 427 bytes
   body: # Production Postgres (Neon)...
         DATABASE_URL="postgresql://neondb_owner:<pw>@ep-...neon.tech/neondb?sslmode=require"
         NEXTAUTH_SECRET="<secret>"
         TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN="<token>" ...
GET /api/media/..%2f..%2fpackage.json    -> HTTP 200  ({"name":"sqb-ai-landing"...})
GET /api/media/..%2f..%2fprisma%2fschema.prisma -> HTTP 200 (4024 bytes)
GET /api/media/doesnotexist.png          -> HTTP 404   (control — proves traversal is the cause)
GET /api/media/..%252f..%252f.env        -> HTTP 404   (double-encoding fails; single decode only)
```
Leaked variable names confirmed across all reviewers: `DATABASE_URL`, `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, `NEXTAUTH_URL`, `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID`.

**Real-world impact.** Complete compromise:
- `DATABASE_URL` → direct read/write/drop on production Neon Postgres (all content + all `ContactSubmission` PII).
- `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` → forge a valid admin JWT session cookie for any admin email → full admin-panel takeover with **no password** (chains to CRITICAL-1b below).
- `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` → hijack the contact bot.

**Deployment nuance (does not reduce severity).** `readImage()` only takes the vulnerable `fs.readFile` branch when **not** Netlify and **not** Vercel-blob. On the documented Netlify primary deployment, `readImage()` uses the blob-store branch where `key` is a blob key (traversal does not apply). On Vercel, media is served from the CDN and this handler isn't the serving path. **But:** the route is unauthenticated and the vulnerable branch is live on local dev and on any plain-Node/Docker/VPS/Railway/Render host. The leaked secrets are real production credentials. Treat as CRITICAL.

**Fix (code-level).**
```ts
// site/lib/storage.ts — at the top of readImage(key)
import path from "node:path";

const UPLOADS_DIR = path.resolve(process.cwd(), "public", "uploads");

// 1) Strict allowlist matching saveImage()'s generated key format: <timestamp>-<uuid>.<ext>
const KEY_RE = /^\d+-[0-9a-f-]{36}\.(jpg|jpeg|png|webp|gif|svg)$/i;
if (!KEY_RE.test(key)) return null;

// 2) Defense-in-depth containment check
const resolved = path.resolve(UPLOADS_DIR, key);
if (resolved !== path.join(UPLOADS_DIR, path.basename(key))) return null;
if (!resolved.startsWith(UPLOADS_DIR + path.sep)) return null;
```
Additionally: prefer a DB/blob-store lookup over touching the filesystem; on Vercel return 404 for this route. **Rotate `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, the Neon `DATABASE_URL` password, and the Telegram bot token now** — they were exposed during this audit.

### 🔴 CRITICAL-1b — Leaked `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` → admin session forgery → full PII access (consequence of CRITICAL-1)

**Where.** `site/lib/auth.ts:29` (`session: { strategy: "jwt", maxAge: 7d }`), `:45` (`secret: process.env.NEXTAUTH_SECRET`); `site/middleware.ts` verifies only the NextAuth JWT; every admin action calls `requireAuth()` which checks only `if (!session) throw`. Submissions render full PII (`name`, `email`, `phone`, `company`, `direction`, `message`) in `site/app/admin/submissions/` (list + `[id]` detail).

**Impact.** Once the secret leaks (CRITICAL-1), an attacker mints a valid admin session JWT for any email, passes middleware, and gains full CRUD across all 10 admin sections plus read of all contact-form PII — without any password.

**Fix.** Fix CRITICAL-1; rotate `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` (invalidates existing sessions); shorten `maxAge`; add a server-side token-version/`issued-at` check so a single rotation reliably revokes forged tokens.

### 🟠 HIGH-1 — No brute-force protection or lockout on admin login

**What it is.** `CredentialsProvider.authorize()` runs only `prisma.adminUser.findUnique` + `bcrypt.compare` with **no attempt counter, no lockout, no backoff, no CAPTCHA**. `/api/auth/*` is not covered by middleware (matcher only guards `/admin/*`). Unlimited online password guessing is possible against known admin usernames.

**Where.** `site/lib/auth.ts:14-26`; `site/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts` (bare handler); `site/middleware.ts:5`.

**Evidence.** No throttling code exists in `authorize()`. The project *knows* the pattern — `site/app/api/contact/route.ts:17-30` implements a 3/min/IP limiter — but deliberately omitted it from login. Default usernames `sqbai@admin1/2/3` are documented.

**Impact.** Unthrottled credential stuffing / brute force against admin accounts; with default seed passwords still active, immediate takeover.

**Fix.** Reuse the existing `checkRateLimit` pattern (durable store, not in-memory Map) keyed on per-IP **and** per-account; add progressive lockout after N failures; add CAPTCHA after repeated failures; consider 2FA for admin.

---

### 🟠 HIGH-2 — Default admin credentials shipped in seed and documented in-repo

**What it is.** `seed.ts` bootstraps three admins with predictable passwords; the same credentials are reproduced verbatim in the checked-in `CLAUDE.md`. No forced first-login rotation.

**Where.** `site/prisma/seed.ts:18-22` (`sqbai@admin1/ChangeMe!2026A`, `…B`, `…C`; bcrypt-hashed cost 10 at `:493`, bootstrap only when `existingAdmins === 0`); `CLAUDE.md:165-170`. `AdminUser` schema (`schema.prisma:12-19`) has no `mustChangePassword`/rotation field.

**Impact.** If production was seeded fresh and never rotated, the admin panel is accessible with publicly-known credentials → full content control + PII access. Credentials are in git history and docs, i.e. effectively public.

**Fix.** Remove plaintext passwords from `seed.ts` and `CLAUDE.md`; generate a random password printed once at seed time (or require an interactive setup step); add a `mustChangePassword` flag enforced on first login; **rotate all deployed admin passwords now**.

### 🟠 HIGH-3 — Contact rate-limit bypass via spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` + unbounded in-memory Map (memory-exhaustion DoS)

**What it is.** The `/api/contact` limiter keys on attacker-controlled headers (`x-nf-client-connection-ip` || first `x-forwarded-for`). Rotating the header per request yields a fresh bucket, defeating the 3/min cap. The backing `Map` is module-global and never evicts keys (only filters timestamps within a key), so distinct spoofed IPs accumulate unboundedly → memory growth. The rate check also runs **before** the honeypot, so bot traffic still populates the Map.

**Where.** `site/app/api/contact/route.ts:19` (`const recentSubmissions = new Map()`), `:21-30` (`checkRateLimit`), `:50-53` (IP from spoofable headers), `:55` (limiter before honeypot at `:73`).

**Proof (live, honeypot set so no real submissions).**
```
Fixed   XFF=9.9.9.9   -> 200,200,200,429,429   (limiter works per-key)
Rotating XFF=10.20.30.1..8 -> 200 x8           (cap fully bypassed)
Rotating x-nf-client-connection-ip 8.8.8.31..35 -> 200 x5 (higher-precedence header also spoofable)
```

**Impact.** Defeats the only abuse control on a public, state-changing endpoint that fires a Telegram message + DB write per accepted request → spam flooding of the owner's Telegram and `ContactSubmission` table, plus unbounded process-memory growth.

**Fix.**
- Derive client IP from a **trusted** platform header only (validate proxy hop count); do not trust raw `x-forwarded-for` on untrusted ingress.
- Move the rate limiter to a shared, bounded TTL/LRU store (Upstash/Redis / Vercel KV).
- Run the honeypot check **before** consuming a limiter slot.
- Add a hard Map size cap as a backstop if keeping in-memory.

### 🟠 HIGH-4 — Missing all HTTP security headers (no CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy)

**What it is.** `next.config.mjs` defines no `headers()`; middleware adds none; `netlify.toml` sets only `Cache-Control`. The app ships zero defense headers. (Reviewers split MEDIUM/HIGH; retained at HIGH because the authenticated admin panel is fully framable and there is no CSP backstop for the SVG-XSS sink.)

**Where.** `site/next.config.mjs:1-24` (no `headers()`); `site/middleware.ts` (auth only); `netlify.toml` (`Cache-Control` only).

**Proof (live).** `curl -D - /` and `/admin/login` return only `X-Powered-By: Next.js` among security-relevant headers. `/admin/login` is framable (no `X-Frame-Options`/`frame-ancestors`).

**Impact.** Clickjacking of admin login / state-changing admin forms; no CSP to neutralize stored XSS; MIME-sniffing on `/api/media`; framework fingerprint leak via `X-Powered-By`.

**Fix.** Add to `site/next.config.mjs`:
```js
const securityHeaders = [
  { key: "Content-Security-Policy", value: "default-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; script-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data: https:" },
  { key: "Strict-Transport-Security", value: "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload" },
  { key: "X-Frame-Options", value: "DENY" },
  { key: "X-Content-Type-Options", value: "nosniff" },
  { key: "Referrer-Policy", value: "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" },
  { key: "Permissions-Policy", value: "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()" },
];
const nextConfig = {
  poweredByHeader: false,
  async headers() { return [{ source: "/:path*", headers: securityHeaders }]; },
  // ...existing config
};
```
Apply a strict `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox` specifically to `/api/media` responses.

---

### 🟠 HIGH-5 — Stored XSS via SVG upload served inline as `image/svg+xml` (no sanitization, no CSP)

**What it is.** The upload endpoint accepts `image/svg+xml` based solely on the client-declared MIME (`file.type`, no magic-byte check, no SVG scrubbing). SVG is an active document format: an uploaded SVG with `<script>` executes JS in the site origin when the asset URL is opened top-level. With no CSP and no `Content-Disposition`/`nosniff`, there is no mitigation.

> Adjudication note: reviewers split between HIGH and MEDIUM. The split is because the upload endpoint **is admin-authenticated** (`getServerSession` → 401 for anonymous), and script execution requires direct navigation to the asset (not `<img src>`). Realistic threat = admin-to-admin pivot, or a logged-in admin lured to a stored-SVG link, or amplification of CRITICAL-1b (forged admin session). Retained as HIGH given the bank domain and absent CSP; treat as **at least** MEDIUM.

**Where.** `site/app/api/admin/upload/route.ts:7-13,32` (ALLOWED includes `image/svg+xml`; checks only `file.type`); `site/lib/storage.ts:20,90-91` (maps `.svg` → `image/svg+xml`); `site/app/api/media/[key]/route.ts:12-17` (serves that Content-Type, only `Cache-Control`, no `Content-Disposition`). No DOMPurify/svgo anywhere.

**Impact.** Script execution in the application origin: admin-action abuse via server actions, defacement, phishing hosted on the bank domain, pivoting against admins.

**Fix.**
- Drop `image/svg+xml` from `ALLOWED`, **or** sanitize server-side with DOMPurify (SVG profile) / a dedicated SVG sanitizer before storing.
- Serve user uploads with `Content-Disposition: attachment`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox`.
- Validate real content (magic bytes) instead of trusting `file.type`.
- Serve user uploads from a separate, cookieless origin/CDN.

## 3. MEDIUM / LOW Findings (concise)

### MEDIUM

- **`/api/track` unauthenticated, unthrottled DB writes (cost/DoS amplification).** `site/app/api/track/route.ts:12-37` — no auth, no rate limit, no honeypot; one `prisma.pageView.create()` per request with attacker-controlled `visitorId/sessionId/path` (length-capped only). `middleware.ts` doesn't cover `/api/*`. Live: repeated anonymous POSTs all return 200, rows persisted (confirmed + cleaned up). Impact bounded to row growth/cost and analytics pollution (no PII/integrity). **Fix:** per-IP rate limit, dedup window on `(visitorId, sessionId, path)`, origin check, consider sampling/batching.

- **`force-dynamic` homepage runs 10 parallel DB queries per request; caching silently disabled.** `site/app/page.tsx:5,34-46` (`force-dynamic` + `Promise.all` of 10 queries, two with relation joins); `site/lib/prisma.ts:24-26` (singleton cached only in non-production). Admin actions call `revalidatePath("/")` everywhere, proving caching was intended — but `force-dynamic` overrides it, making those calls no-ops. **Fix:** remove `force-dynamic` and rely on `revalidatePath("/")` invalidation, or wrap reads in `unstable_cache` with tag-based revalidation; use the Neon pooler; collapse queries.

- **No PII retention / minimization / consent.** `ContactSubmission` (`schema.prisma:129-141`) and `PageView` (`:117-127`) retain identifiable PII and tracking IDs indefinitely; no TTL/purge job, no consent gate on `/api/track`, no erasure/export path beyond manual admin delete. **Fix:** define retention windows + scheduled purge; add consent + privacy notice for tracking; document subject-access/erasure; minimize/hash tracking IDs.

- **Contact handler awaits Telegram fetch with no timeout before DB write.** `site/app/api/contact/route.ts:120-132` (`fetch` to Telegram, no `AbortController`/timeout), then `:141-152` DB write. A slow/down Telegram stalls the invocation for the full platform timeout. (One reviewer adjudicated LOW given the per-IP limiter and that no DB connection is held during the wait.) **Fix:** wrap Telegram fetch in a 3–5s `AbortController` timeout (non-fatal); persist to DB first, then fire-and-forget the notification (`waitUntil`/queue).

- **No magic-byte validation on uploads (MIME trusted from client).** `site/app/api/admin/upload/route.ts:32` validates against `file.type` (spoofable); on-disk extension derived from spoofable MIME. Same root cause as HIGH-5; **Fix:** verify magic bytes against claimed MIME.

### LOW

- **Flat admin privilege model (no RBAC).** All 10 `admin/*/actions.ts` use an identical `requireAuth()` that only checks session presence; JWT/session carry only `id`; `AdminUser` has no `role` field. Single-tenant-by-design (3 equally-trusted admins), so this is a hardening/least-privilege gap, not an exploitable flaw. **Fix (only if admin base grows):** add a `role` field, include it in the JWT, gate destructive/PII actions.

- **`createProject` trusts client-supplied primary-key `id`; `direction`/`status` stored as unvalidated free-text.** `site/app/admin/projects/actions.ts:54-57,68-69`; `queries.ts:29-30` casts raw strings to enum types with `as` (compile-time only). Admin-gated, Prisma-parameterized (no injection), React-escaped (no XSS) — data-quality/robustness gap. **Fix:** Zod-validate `id` format/uniqueness and constrain `direction`/`status` to the known unions; replace `as` casts with runtime narrowing.

- **Login username-enumeration timing oracle.** `site/lib/auth.ts:20` returns before bcrypt for unknown emails vs. running `bcrypt.compare` for known ones. Network-noise-dominated, theoretical. **Fix:** always run a dummy `bcrypt.compare` against a fixed hash on the not-found path (constant-work).

## 4. Reliability & Scale

### What happens when hundreds fill the form / load the site at once?

**Homepage load (read path).** Every homepage hit is `force-dynamic` and runs `Promise.all` of **10 Neon queries** (`page.tsx:5,34-46`), two with relation joins, with **no ISR / `unstable_cache` / revalidate window**. Content that changes rarely is refetched on every single request. In production, `PrismaClient` is **not** cached on `globalThis` (`prisma.ts:24-26` only caches when `NODE_ENV !== "production"`), so each cold serverless instance instantiates a fresh client and opens new Neon WebSocket connections. Net effect: **~10× read amplification per visitor**, plus cold-start Prisma-engine + Neon-handshake latency on the first request of each instance.

**Form submit / tracking (write path).** `/api/contact` and `/api/track` each perform synchronous DB writes per request with no queue or backpressure. `/api/track` has **no rate limit at all**; `/api/contact`'s limiter is **bypassable** (HIGH-3) and `/api/contact` also blocks on a no-timeout Telegram fetch before writing. Under a burst of submissions while Telegram is degraded, invocations pile up.

### Breaking point & bottlenecks

- **Breaking point (from load test):** ~**50 concurrent connections**.
- **Primary bottleneck:** **Neon connection pool** — the combination of `force-dynamic` 10-query fan-out, per-instance PrismaClient (no pooled singleton in prod), and unthrottled write endpoints exhausts Neon's connection ceiling. Once exhausted, the homepage, contact handler, and admin **all** start returning 500s (the homepage was already observed returning 500 when the DB path failed).
- **Secondary amplifiers:** unauthenticated `/api/track` flooding, synchronous Telegram fetch with no timeout, no homepage caching.

### Fix roadmap

1. **Caching / ISR (biggest win, lowest effort):** drop `force-dynamic` on the homepage; rely on the already-wired `revalidatePath("/")` admin invalidation, or wrap each read in `unstable_cache` with tags. This removes ~10× read amplification on the hottest route.
2. **Connection pooling:** use the **Neon pooler / PgBouncer (transaction mode)** connection string for serverless; keep `PrismaClient` a true singleton (cache on `globalThis` in production too). Collapse the 10 queries into a single `prisma.$transaction` or fewer combined queries; add per-query timeouts.
3. **Rate-limit redesign:** replace the in-memory Map with a shared bounded store (Upstash/Redis / Vercel KV); key on a **trusted** platform IP; apply to `/api/track` and `/api/auth/callback/credentials` as well as `/api/contact`; run honeypot before the limiter.
4. **Queue / async the side effects:** persist contact submissions to the DB first (source of truth), then enqueue the Telegram notification (background queue / `waitUntil`) so the response is never blocked on the upstream; add an `AbortController` timeout on the Telegram fetch.
5. **Tracking write reduction:** dedup/sample `PageView` writes, batch via `createMany`, or move analytics to an append-optimized sink / edge KV; add a retention/TTL purge job.

## 5. Prioritized Remediation Checklist

Ordered by **risk ÷ effort** — hand to an engineer top-down.

| # | Action | Severity | Effort | Files |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Rotate ALL secrets now** — Neon `DATABASE_URL` password, `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`. Assume compromised. | CRITICAL | Low | `.env` / hosting env |
| 2 | **Fix path traversal** in `readImage()` — strict key allowlist regex + `path.resolve` containment check; 404 on Vercel. | CRITICAL | Low | `lib/storage.ts:77`, `app/api/media/[key]/route.ts:8` |
| 3 | **Rotate default admin passwords**; remove plaintext creds from `seed.ts` + `CLAUDE.md`; add `mustChangePassword`. | HIGH | Low | `prisma/seed.ts:18-22`, `CLAUDE.md`, `schema.prisma` |
| 4 | **Add security headers** (`headers()` in `next.config.mjs`: CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy) + `poweredByHeader: false`. | HIGH | Low | `next.config.mjs` |
| 5 | **Harden SVG uploads** — drop `image/svg+xml` or sanitize (DOMPurify); serve uploads with `Content-Disposition: attachment` + nosniff; validate magic bytes. | HIGH | Med | `app/api/admin/upload/route.ts`, `lib/storage.ts`, `app/api/media/[key]/route.ts` |
| 6 | **Add brute-force protection** on `/api/auth` (per-IP + per-account lockout/backoff via durable store; CAPTCHA after N). | HIGH | Med | `lib/auth.ts`, new limiter util |
| 7 | **Redesign rate limiting** — trusted IP source, shared bounded TTL store, honeypot-before-limiter; apply to `/api/contact`, `/api/track`, login. | HIGH | Med | `app/api/contact/route.ts`, `app/api/track/route.ts` |
| 8 | **Throttle `/api/track`** (rate limit + dedup window + origin check). | MEDIUM | Low | `app/api/track/route.ts` |
| 9 | **Fix homepage scale** — remove `force-dynamic`, enable ISR/`unstable_cache`; Neon pooler; singleton Prisma in prod; collapse queries. | MEDIUM | Med | `app/page.tsx`, `lib/prisma.ts`, `lib/queries.ts` |
| 10 | **Async the Telegram fetch** with timeout + DB-first persistence (queue/`waitUntil`). | MEDIUM | Med | `app/api/contact/route.ts:120-152` |
| 11 | **PII governance** — retention windows + purge job, tracking consent, erasure/export process, field minimization. | MEDIUM | Med | `schema.prisma`, new cron/job |
| 12 | **Input validation** — Zod-validate `createProject` id + enum-constrain `direction`/`status`; replace `as` casts with runtime narrowing. | LOW | Low | `app/admin/projects/actions.ts`, `lib/queries.ts` |
| 13 | **Constant-time auth** (dummy bcrypt on not-found) + consider RBAC if admin base grows. | LOW | Low | `lib/auth.ts`, `schema.prisma` |

**Do items 1–2 before anything else and before the next deploy.** They are the difference between a hardening backlog and an active, unauthenticated full-compromise primitive.
